# PostgreSQL 2TB Migration Plan: On-Prem → Managed Cloud

1. **Pre-migration planning & environment prep** — Provision the target managed cloud database (matching PostgreSQL major/minor version and required extensions), size compute/storage for 2 TB plus growth headroom, configure networking (VPC peering, security groups, DNS), and set up monitoring/alerting on both source and target instances.

2. **Initial stakeholder & user communication** — Notify engineering stakeholders, support teams, and all ~4,000 DAU at least 3–5 days ahead of the Sunday maintenance window, stating the date/time, expected 2-hour duration, and user-facing impact (e.g., read-only or full outage). Post to a status page.

3. **Establish continuous replication** — Configure logical replication/CDC (native PostgreSQL logical replication, `pglogical`, or a managed migration/DMS service) from the on-prem primary to the cloud target so changes stream continuously ahead of cutover, minimizing the final sync window.

4. **Full production backup (safety baseline)** — Take a full, verified physical or logical backup (`pg_basebackup` with WAL archiving, supplemented by `pg_dump`/`pg_dumpall` for schema/globals) of the production database, and confirm it restores successfully. **No step that could modify or risk production data may proceed until this backup is confirmed valid.**

5. **Dry run / rehearsal on non-production data** — Restore the backup from Step 4 into a staging environment and execute the entire planned migration and cutover procedure end-to-end (replication setup, catch-up, cutover scripts, connection-string swap, verification queries) against this non-production copy. Time each step to confirm the full process fits within the 2-hour window; fix any defects found and re-rehearse if needed.

6. **Go/No-Go review & reminder communication** — Review rehearsal results, current replication lag, backup validity, and rollback readiness with stakeholders 1–2 days before the window; confirm go-ahead. Re-notify users 24 hours and again 1 hour before the maintenance window begins.

7. **Enter maintenance window & final safety backup** — At the start of the Sunday window, put the application into maintenance/read-only mode to stop new writes on-prem, then immediately take a final incremental backup/snapshot capturing the exact pre-cutover state. This backup, together with the untouched on-prem server, is the basis for rollback.

8. **Final sync & cutover** — Allow logical replication to drain to zero lag, verify no pending WAL/transactions remain, stop replication, then repoint application connection strings/DNS to the managed cloud instance and run any needed post-migration reconciliation (e.g., resetting sequences to correct values).

9. **Data integrity verification** — Compare source and target via row counts per table, checksums/hash aggregates (e.g., `pg_checksums`, per-table `md5`/`sum` hash comparisons), and spot-check key business metrics; run automated smoke tests against critical application workflows before reopening to users.

10. **Rollback procedure (contingency)** — If verification in Step 9 fails or a critical defect surfaces, immediately revert application connection strings/DNS back to the on-prem server (kept fully intact and untouched since Step 7), restoring from the Step 7 backup only if the on-prem instance itself was altered; notify stakeholders of the rollback and root-cause the issue before scheduling a re-attempt.

11. **Resume operations & completion communication** — Once verification passes, take the application out of maintenance mode, closely monitor performance/error rates and replication health for the following hours, and send a completion/status update to stakeholders and users confirming service restoration.

12. **Post-migration monitoring & decommission** — Monitor the new production database for 48–72 hours (performance, error rates, connection health), keep the on-prem server intact and untouched as a fallback throughout this period, then decommission it only after stability is confirmed and stakeholders sign off.

STEP COUNT: 12
